outcome: File and object services run on the platform already in place, sparing the media operation a second storage refresh and support contract.
overview: A media operation that has already consolidated its virtual machines onto a hyperconverged platform usually still runs separate file and object storage, which means a second refresh cycle, a second support relationship and capacity that cannot be shared. Nutanix Files and Objects serve both from the same cluster, so unstructured storage grows within the platform already there. Whether this beats dedicated scale-out storage depends on the volume and the access pattern, and that comparison should be made rather than taken for granted.

benefits.text: File and object services run on the platform already deployed rather than on separate systems
benefits.limits: Consolidation is attractive at moderate volume; at petabyte scale a dedicated scale-out platform usually wins and the comparison should be run

benefits.text: Capacity is shared with the virtual machine estate rather than stranded in a separate array
benefits.limits: Sharing means unstructured growth consumes capacity the virtual machine estate may need; the growth plan has to account for both

benefits.text: One platform, one lifecycle and one support relationship instead of two
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance rather than from host counts or invoice history; a design built on the latter is a quotation with an architecture attached

residency: Content remains on customer-owned nodes in the customer data centre

notFor.situation: A petabyte-scale media archive with sustained high-throughput access
notFor.why: Dedicated scale-out storage is designed for that profile and generally wins on cost per terabyte at scale

notFor.situation: An estate not already running this hyperconverged platform
notFor.why: The value is in consolidating onto a platform that already exists

3) Deploy — file and object services established and presented
4) Migrate and hand over — workloads migrated, separate systems retired, operations handed over
